It also says CKL's dual-monitor model that does have EDID emulation (622DP-5) costs $379 and has HDMI outputs, not DisplayPort.
standout_why: I read the cited TESmart page's ranking (the TESmart page itself returned HTTP 429), tradingdeskgear.com, gearexplained.com/guides/dual-monitor-kvm-switch, dockgearhq.com and streamingjet.com. None of them mentions the CKL 622DP-4 or CKL's EDID limit. tradingdeskgear already says the Level1Techs switch doesn't emulate monitors. gearexplained already says AV Access's 8KSW21DP-DM has no EDID emulation. dockgearhq covers the StarTech P2DD46A2 (DP 1.2), not the P2CDD143 that ChatGPT showed. No rival names the CKL 622DP-5 or the 622DP-MST, which runs both screens at 4K60 together.
decides: ChatGPT told shoppers to prioritize EDID emulation, then picked the CKL 622DP-4 as its budget pick. CKL's own page says that switch has no EDID emulation. The other DP-to-DP switches under $200 that I priced don't have it either: AV Access 8KSW21DP-DM ($159.99, 'does not support EDID emulation at present') and CKL 622DP-MST ($169). CKL's EDID model costs $379 and drives the monitors over HDMI. So the budget tier only works if the shopper accepts windows rearranging. Our AV Access KD-E10 ($169.99) has EDID emulation but outputs HDMI 2.0b and tops out at dual 4K60. A shopper who needs EDID emulation on DisplayPort monitors is in the TESmart DKS202-M24 price range (tradingdeskgear lists $329.90) or higher.
